newsitem.title: CAMBODIA: Hardline Khmer Rouge rebels kill four in village.
newsitem.headline: Hardline Khmer Rouge rebels kill four in village.

text.p: Khmer Rouge hardliners killed four people and injured seven in an attack on a village in central Cambodia, a government official said on Tuesday.
Interior Ministry spokesman Sok Phal said about 30 men, whom he identified as Khmer Rouge rebels, entered the village in the the central province of Kampong Chhnang late on Friday searching for food.
The rebels killed one policeman, two government soldiers and one civilian during the attack, he said.
The Khmer Rouge have been at war with the government since the group reneged on a peace treaty signed with rival groups in 1991 to bring an end to fighting.
Khmer Rouge hardliners loyal to rebel leader Pol Pot have carried out similar attacks in the past in quests for food.
In August, former top Khmer Rouge official Ieng Sary broke with the hardliners, taking several thousand supporters with him.
Ieng Sary's followers, sometimes backed by government troops, have engaged in skirmishes with hardline rebels since then.
The Khmer Rouge ruled Cambodia between 1975 and 1979, during which more than one million people died by execution, disease or overwork.
